key_insight: NeoGx uses early NICU electronic health record data to flag neonates most likely to need genetic evaluation, helping target rapid genome sequencing to the right infants sooner.
clinical_relevance: If implemented well, this approach could shorten time to genetic workup and diagnosis for critically ill newborns who may benefit from earlier answers and management.
method: Trained a machine learning model on structured EHR data plus phenotypes from clinical notes.
Used 14,272 Level IV NICU patients split into development, calibration, and independent validation cohorts.
Evaluated predictions over the first 4 NICU weeks for genetic evaluation within 18 months of life.
evidence_signal: In independent validation, NeoGx achieved ROC AUC 0.849 and PR AUC 0.771; model-guided referral reduced mean time to first genetic evaluation from 44 to 29 days.
watch_item: This is a retrospective, single-system EHR-based model, so performance and workflow impact may differ across NICUs, data systems, and referral practices.
paper_title: NeoGx: Machine-Recommended Rapid Genome Sequencing for Neonates
